newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African serial killer suspect appears in court.
newsitem.headline: S.African serial killer suspect appears in court.

text.p: A South African serial killer suspect appeared in court on Monday and was expected to face charges of murdering at least 19 women, police said.
Sipho Thwala, 30, is prime suspect in the murders, in which the victims were strangled in sugar cane fields on the outskirts of the Indian Ocean port city over the past three years.
He appeared in ragged clothing in a regional magistrate's court on Monday, but no charges were put to him and he was remanded in custody until September 2, pending further investigations.
Thwala, who made his living selling sugar cane, lived with his mother in a shack in sprawling KwaMashu black township near Durban, where he was arrested late last week.
Investigating officer Philip Veldhuizen told reporters that other murders under investigation might also be found to be linked to the case.
"There might be more cases as I carry on investigating other murders that were committed in the area for links to the way these victims were killed," he told reporters.
The court forbade reporters to print photographs of the suspect or release descriptions of him, because he still has to appear in identity parades.
In just over two years at least six other serial killer cases have emerged in South Africa. In one of them, a man is on trial for the murders of 38 women in the industrial heartland.
